chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever has the weight of a mustard seed of tribal chauvinism ('asabiyya) in his heart, God Almighty will raise him on the Day of Resurrection with the bedouins of the Age of Ignorance.

key_terms.أَعْرَابُ الْجَاهِلِيَّة: Bedouins of the Jahiliyya: Arab nomads of the pre-Islamic era, paradigmatic of ignorance and tribal values in classical Islamic thought
key_terms.عَصَبِيَّة: 'Asabiyya: tribal chauvinism, racial partisanship, group solidarity based on ethnicity or clan that leads to injustice
key_terms.مِثْقَالُ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ: Weight of a mustard seed: a Quranic idiom for the smallest conceivable amount (cf. 99:7-8)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about 'asabiyya (tribal chauvinism) in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warns in the strongest terms against 'asabiyya — tribal or racial partisanship — stating that even the smallest amount of it in one's heart (comparable to a mustard seed) will result in being resurrected alongside the pagan Arab bedouins of the pre-Islamic era. This saying addressed a society where tribal pride was the dominant social force, and the Prophet is radically repudiating that value system. The punishment of being raised with the people of Jahiliyya — those who had not accepted Islam and whose tribal ways were considered the opposite of the Islamic ideal — reflects the gravity of this vice.
